question: The 11th Fundamental Duty provides opportunities for education for the ______ age group of children.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6-14.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 11th Fundamental Duty [Article 51A(k)] makes it the duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years. (6–14 वर्ष)

• It was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, the same amendment that inserted Article 21A (Right to Education) as a Fundamental Right.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties are contained in Part IV-A, Article 51A of the Constitution of India.

• Originally ten duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee; the eleventh was added in 2002, making the present total eleven.

• The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia).

NOTE

• Article 21A guarantees free and compulsory education to all children aged 6–14 years; it was operationalised through the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, effective from 1 April 2010.

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts.

question: As per the Census of India 2011, which Union Territory recorded the lowest population growth rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshadweep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, Lakshadweep recorded the lowest decadal population growth rate (2001–2011) among the Union Territories, at about 6.3%. (लक्षद्वीप)

• Lakshadweep also has the smallest population of all States and Union Territories — about 64,473 persons.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Among the UTs in 2011, Dadra and Nagar Haveli recorded the highest decadal growth (about 55.9%), followed by Daman and Diu (about 53.8%).

• Delhi grew by about 21.2% and Chandigarh by about 17.2%.

• Among the States, Nagaland was the only one to record a negative growth rate (-0.6%) in 2011, while Meghalaya had the highest (27.9%).

NOTE

• Census 2011 highlights: total population 121.08 crore; sex ratio 943; literacy rate 74.04%; density 382 persons/km².

• The Census of India was first conducted (non-synchronously) in 1872 under Lord Mayo; the first synchronous census was in 1881 under Lord Ripon. Census 2011 was the 15th national census.

question: In which year were the Arms Act and Vernacular Press Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1878.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both the Indian Arms Act and the Vernacular Press Act were passed in 1878 during the viceroyalty of Lord Lytton. (लॉर्ड लिटन, 1878)

◦ The Vernacular Press Act, 1878 was aimed at controlling Indian-language (vernacular) newspapers that criticised British rule; it was nicknamed the "Gagging Act".

◦ The Indian Arms Act, 1878 forbade Indians from keeping arms without a licence, while Europeans were exempted.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lord Lytton (1876–1880) is also associated with the Delhi Durbar of 1877 (proclaiming Queen Victoria as Kaiser-i-Hind), the abolition of import duties on British cotton, and the reduction of the maximum age for the Civil Services examination from 21 to 19 years.

• The Vernacular Press Act was repealed in 1882 by Lord Ripon, who is known as the "Father of Local Self-Government" in India.

• Amrita Bazar Patrika famously converted itself overnight into an English newspaper to escape the Vernacular Press Act.

NOTE

• Other important press regulations: Censorship of Press Act 1799 (Lord Wellesley), Licensing Regulations 1823 (John Adams), Metcalfe Act 1835 (Metcalfe was called the "Liberator of the Indian Press"), Newspaper Act 1908 and Indian Press Act 1910.

question: In which state of India is Kaziranga National Park located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kaziranga National Park is located in the Golaghat and Nagaon districts of Assam, on the floodplains of the Brahmaputra river. (काजीरंगा राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — असम)

• It is world-famous for hosting about two-thirds of the world's population of the one-horned Indian rhinoceros.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kaziranga was declared a National Park in 1974, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985, and a Tiger Reserve in 2006; it has the highest density of tigers among protected areas in the world.

• It is also an Important Bird Area recognised by BirdLife International, and is home to the "Big Five" of Kaziranga — rhinoceros, tiger, elephant, wild water buffalo and swamp deer (barasingha).

• Other national parks of Assam: Manas (also a World Heritage Site), Nameri, Orang and Dibru-Saikhowa.

NOTE

• Options for comparison — Gujarat: Gir National Park (Asiatic lion); Karnataka: Bandipur, Nagarhole (Rajiv Gandhi) National Park; West Bengal: Sundarbans National Park (Royal Bengal tiger), Jaldapara, Neora Valley.

question: Whose autobiography is titled ‘Ace against Odds’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sania Mirza.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ace against Odds" (2016) is the autobiography of the Indian tennis star Sania Mirza, co-written with her father Imran Mirza and journalist Shivani Gupta. It was released by the then Prime Minister-level dignitaries and covers her rise in international tennis. (सानिया मिर्ज़ा की आत्मकथा)

• The word "ace" in tennis means a serve that the opponent fails to touch, which makes the title a pun on her sport.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sania Mirza reached World No. 1 in women's doubles (2015) and won six Grand Slam titles (three women's doubles and three mixed doubles). She has received the Arjuna Award (2004), Padma Shri (2006), Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2015) and Padma Bhushan (2016).

• Autobiographies of the other options: Saina Nehwal — "Playing to Win"; Mary Kom — "Unbreakable"; Mirabai Chanu is the weightlifter who won a silver medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

NOTE

• Other sports autobiographies frequently asked: "Playing It My Way" (Sachin Tendulkar), "A Century Is Not Enough" (Sourav Ganguly), "The Test of My Life" (Yuvraj Singh), "Straight from the Heart" (Kapil Dev), "Race of My Life" (Milkha Singh).

question: By what name are the flat membrane-enclosed sacs present in the Golgi apparatus known?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cisternae.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Golgi apparatus (Golgi complex/body) consists of stacks of flat, membrane-enclosed sacs called "cisternae", along with associated vesicles and tubules. (सिस्टर्नी)

• Each stack usually contains 4–8 cisternae, arranged with a cis (forming) face near the endoplasmic reticulum and a trans (maturing) face towards the plasma membrane.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Golgi apparatus was discovered by Camillo Golgi in 1898; it is called the "post office" or "secretory/packaging organelle" of the cell.

• Functions: modification, sorting, packaging and dispatch of proteins and lipids; formation of lysosomes; synthesis of cell wall material in plants; glycosylation of proteins.

NOTE

• Option 1 "Lamellae" — the flattened membranous plates found in chloroplasts (also, thin plate-like layers in bone).

• Option 3 "Cristae" — the infoldings of the inner membrane of the mitochondrion, which increase surface area for ATP production.

• Option 4 "Stroma" — the colourless fluid matrix of the chloroplast in which the dark reaction (Calvin cycle) occurs.

• In plant cells the Golgi bodies are called dictyosomes.

question: The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY) was launched in the year ________ by Government of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1997.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) was launched on 1 December 1997 by the Government of India (Ministry of Urban Affairs & Employment). (स्वर्ण जयंती शहरी रोजगार योजना, 1997)

• Its objective was to provide gainful employment to the urban unemployed and underemployed poor, through self-employment ventures and wage employment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• SJSRY subsumed three earlier urban poverty-alleviation schemes: the Nehru Rozgar Yojana (NRY), the Urban Basic Services for the Poor (UBSP) and the Prime Minister's Integrated Urban Poverty Eradication Programme (PMIUPEP).

• It had two main components — the Urban Self-Employment Programme (USEP) and the Urban Wage Employment Programme (UWEP); it was funded on a 75:25 Centre–State basis.

• SJSRY was restructured in 2009 and finally replaced in 2013 by the National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM), which became the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – NULM (DAY-NULM) in 2016.

NOTE

• The word "Swarna Jayanti" (Golden Jubilee) marks the 50th anniversary of India's independence (1947–1997). The corresponding rural scheme was the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), launched in 1999.

question: Manna Dey was a famous personality of India in the field of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Manna Dey (born Prabodh Chandra Dey, 1919–2013) was one of India's greatest playback singers, celebrated for his mastery of Indian classical music as well as light and film songs. (संगीत — पार्श्वगायक)

• He sang more than 3,500 songs in Hindi, Bengali and several other languages over a career spanning five decades.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Famous songs: "Laga Chunari Mein Daag", "Poocho Na Kaise Maine Rain Bitayi", "Ae Meri Zohra Jabeen", "Zindagi Kaisi Hai Paheli" and "Yeh Raat Bheegi Bheegi".

• Awards: Padma Shri (1971), Padma Bhushan (2005), Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2007) and two National Film Awards for Best Male Playback Singer.

• He learnt music from his uncle Krishna Chandra Dey and from Ustad Aman Ali Khan and Ustad Abdul Rahman Khan.

NOTE

• The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in cinema, instituted in 1969; the first recipient was Devika Rani.

• Other legendary playback singers honoured with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award: Lata Mangeshkar (1989), Bhupen Hazarika (1992), Asha Bhosle (2000), Yash Chopra, and lyricist Majrooh Sultanpuri (1993).

question: ‘Chapchar Kut’ is a festival from the state of _________. It is celebrated during March after the completion of the most arduous task of Jhum operation i.e., jungle clearing (clearing of the remnants of burning).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chapchar Kut" is the most important spring festival of Mizoram, celebrated in March after the completion of jhum (shifting) cultivation work — the clearing and burning of jungle patches. (चापचार कुट — मिज़ोरम)

• The highlight of the festival is the famous bamboo dance "Cheraw", along with community feasting, singing and dances such as Khuallam, Chheihlam and Sarlamkai.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Mizoram: Mim Kut (maize festival, celebrated in August–September) and Pawl Kut (harvest festival, in December).

• Jhum cultivation (slash-and-burn / shifting agriculture) is widely practised in North-East India; it is called Podu in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, Kumari in Kerala and Bewar/Dahiya in Madhya Pradesh.

NOTE

• Festivals of the other options — Nagaland: Hornbill Festival (December, the "Festival of Festivals"), Sekrenyi, Moatsu; Jharkhand: Sarhul, Karma, Tusu Parab; Chhattisgarh: Bastar Dussehra, Madai, Hareli.

• Mizoram became the 23rd state of India in 1987; its capital is Aizawl.

question: In which event at the 2023 ISSF Junior World Cup Championships did Amanpreet Singh win a gold medal for India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Men's 25 m pistol.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the 2023 ISSF Junior World Cup, the Indian shooter Amanpreet Singh won the gold medal in the Men's 25 m pistol event. (अमनप्रीत सिंह — 25 मीटर पिस्टल)

• The 25 m pistol event combines a precision stage and a rapid-fire stage, and is one of the standard ISSF pistol disciplines.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation), founded in 1907, has its headquarters in Munich, Germany; it governs Olympic shooting events.

• The ISSF Junior World Cup is a global competition for shooters in the junior age category, where India has consistently topped the medal tally in recent years.

• Indian shooting is administered by the National Rifle Association of India (NRAI), established in 1951.

NOTE

• Famous Indian shooters: Abhinav Bindra (India's first individual Olympic gold, 10 m air rifle, Beijing 2008), Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore (silver, double trap, Athens 2004), Gagan Narang, Vijay Kumar (silver, 25 m rapid fire pistol, London 2012), Manu Bhaker and Saurabh Chaudhary.

question: In which of the following States was the 2023 World Squash Championship held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 2023 World Squash Championship was hosted in India in the state of Tamil Nadu, at Chennai, which has emerged as the country's principal centre for international squash. (तमिलनाडु — चेन्नई)

• Chennai's Indian Squash Academy and the Express Avenue glass court have staged several World Squash Federation (WSF) events.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Squash is a racquet sport played by two (singles) or four (doubles) players in a four-walled court with a small hollow rubber ball.

• The sport is governed worldwide by the World Squash Federation (WSF), founded in 1967, headquartered at Hastings, England; in India it is governed by the Squash Rackets Federation of India (SRFI), based in Chennai.

• Squash has been included in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games programme.

NOTE

• Leading Indian squash players: Saurav Ghosal, Dipika Pallikal Karthik, Joshna Chinappa, Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh. At the 2022 Commonwealth Games (Birmingham) Saurav Ghosal won India's first-ever singles medal (bronze) in squash; at the 2023 Asian Games (Hangzhou) India won gold in the men's team event and in mixed doubles.

question: Mumtaz Khan was named ‘FIH Women’s Rising Star of the Year’ in 2022. She plays which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hockey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mumtaz Khan, a forward from Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, was named the "FIH Women's Rising Star of the Year" for 2021–22. She plays hockey. (हॉकी)

• She was the top scorer for India at the FIH Junior Women's Hockey World Cup 2022 in Potchefstroom, South Africa, where India finished fourth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• FIH stands for the Fédération Internationale de Hockey (International Hockey Federation), founded in 1924, with headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland.

• Other Indian winners of FIH awards: Vivek Sagar Prasad (Rising Star, men, 2019 & 2021), Savita Punia (Goalkeeper of the Year 2021–22), Harmanpreet Singh (FIH Player of the Year 2020–21 and 2021–22), PR Sreejesh (Goalkeeper of the Year 2020–21 and 2021–22).

NOTE

• Hockey is India's most successful Olympic team sport — 8 gold medals (1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, 1980) plus bronze at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 (men).

• Major Dhyan Chand is called "The Wizard/Magician of Hockey"; 29 August, his birthday, is celebrated as National Sports Day.

question: Which of the following is a common financial service provided by Micro Finance Institutions?
option_2: Investment advisory services for high-net-worth individuals
option_4: Small loans to low-income individuals for entrepreneurial activities
solution_text:
The correct answer is Small loans to low-income individuals for entrepreneurial activities.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) provide small-value loans (microcredit) and other basic financial services to low-income households and small entrepreneurs who have no access to formal banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थान)

• Typical features: small loan amounts, no collateral, group/joint-liability lending (Self Help Groups and Joint Liability Groups), doorstep service and frequent repayment instalments.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 describe services of commercial banks, wealth-management firms and card issuers, which serve better-off customers — the opposite of the microfinance target group.

• In India, MFIs are largely regulated by the Reserve Bank of India as NBFC-MFIs; NABARD promotes the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (started 1992), the world's largest microfinance programme.

• SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India) supports MFIs through the SIDBI Foundation for Micro Credit (SFMC).

NOTE

• The concept of modern microfinance was pioneered by Prof. Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh, founder of the Grameen Bank; he and the bank shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

• Related Indian schemes for small borrowers: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (2015) — Shishu, Kishore and Tarun categories — and the Stand-Up India scheme.

question: The Rathwas, who dwell in the state of ___________, perform the Rathwa dance on the occasion of Holi (festival of colours).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rathwas are a tribal community living mainly in the Chhota Udepur and Panchmahal region of eastern Gujarat. They perform the Rathwa (Rathwa ni Gher) dance during Holi. (गुजरात — राठवा जनजाति)

• The dance is performed by men and women in colourful costumes to the beat of drums, marking the arrival of spring and the tribal new year.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Rathwas are also famous for their ritual wall paintings known as "Pithora paintings", made to honour the deity Pithora Baba; Pithora painting has been recognised for its distinct tribal art tradition.

• Other folk dances of Gujarat: Garba, Dandiya Raas, Tippani, Padhar, Bhavai, Hudo and Dangi.

NOTE

• Folk dances of the other options — Andhra Pradesh: Kuchipudi (classical), Veeranatyam, Butta Bommalu, Dhimsa; Telangana: Perini Shivatandavam, Lambadi, Gussadi; Maharashtra: Lavani, Tamasha, Dhangari Gaja, Koli, Powada.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for a governor for each state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 153.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 153 of the Constitution of India provides that "there shall be a Governor for each State". A proviso added by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956, allows the same person to be appointed Governor for two or more States. (अनुच्छेद 153)

• The Governor is the constitutional head of the State and also acts as an agent of the Central Government.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Related Articles: Article 154 (executive power of the State vested in the Governor), Article 155 (appointment of the Governor by the President), Article 156 (term of office — holds office during the pleasure of the President, normally 5 years), Article 157 (qualifications — must be a citizen of India and have completed 35 years of age), Article 158 (conditions of office), Article 161 (pardoning power), Article 213 (power to promulgate ordinances).

• Article 173 deals with the qualifications for membership of a State Legislature.

NOTE

• The office of the Governor is modelled on the Government of India Act, 1935, and on the Canadian pattern of appointment by the Centre.

• The Governor takes the oath administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court of the State concerned (Article 159).

question: Who was the first Woman President of Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annie Besant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress at its Calcutta session in 1917. (एनी बेसेंट, 1917)

• She was of Irish origin and thus the first woman as well as the first foreign-born woman to head the Congress.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Congress (Kanpur session, 1925); she is called the "Nightingale of India (Bharat Kokila)" and became the first woman Governor of an Indian state (United Provinces, 1947).

• Annie Besant founded the Home Rule League in 1916 (Madras) along with Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Pune); she also led the Theosophical Society and founded the Central Hindu College, Varanasi, which later grew into Banaras Hindu University. She started the newspapers "New India" and "Commonweal".

• Aruna Asaf Ali was the heroine of the Quit India Movement (1942) who hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank; Usha Mehta ran the underground Congress Radio during the same movement.

NOTE

• Other Congress "firsts": W. C. Bonnerjee — first President (Bombay, 1885); Dadabhai Naoroji — first Parsi President; Badruddin Tyabji — first Muslim President (1887); George Yule — first English President (1888); Nellie Sengupta — third woman President (1933).

question: _____________ was a star of the Kathak dance form described as ‘Nritya Samragini’ (the empress of dance) by Rabindranath Tagore.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitara Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sitara Devi (1920–2014) was a legendary exponent of the Kathak dance form. Rabindranath Tagore honoured her with the title "Nritya Samragini" — the empress of dance. (सितारा देवी — नृत्य साम्राज्ञी)

• Born in Kolkata to a Banaras-gharana family, she began performing as a child and later dominated Kathak for decades; she also appeared in Hindi films such as Judwa, Roti and Mother India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Awards received by Sitara Devi: Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1969), Padma Shri (1973) and the Kalidas Samman (1995). She famously declined the Padma Bhushan, saying it was inadequate recognition for her contribution.

• Option 2 Rukmini Devi Arundale — revived Bharatanatyam and founded Kalakshetra (Chennai, 1936).

• Options 3 and 4 — Mrinalini Sarabhai and her daughter Mallika Sarabhai are exponents of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi, associated with the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts, Ahmedabad.

NOTE

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh); its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh. Other famous Kathak dancers: Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj, Damayanti Joshi and Uma Sharma.

• India's eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following methods is used to calculate national income by summing up the total spending on final goods and services in an economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Expenditure method.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Expenditure method measures national income by adding up all the final expenditure on goods and services produced within an economy during a year. (व्यय विधि)

◦ Formula: GDP = C + I + G + (X − M), where C = private final consumption expenditure, I = gross domestic capital formation (investment), G = government final consumption expenditure, X = exports and M = imports.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Value-added / Product (Output) method: adds the value added by each producing unit (value of output minus intermediate consumption) across all sectors, avoiding double counting.

• Income method: adds all factor incomes — rent, wages/compensation of employees, interest, profit and mixed income of the self-employed — earned in producing the national product.

• All three methods must theoretically give the same national income figure.

NOTE

• Key aggregates: GDP (Gross Domestic Product), NDP = GDP − Depreciation, GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad, NNP at factor cost = National Income.

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). The first attempt to estimate national income was by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (1867–68); the first scientific estimate was by Prof. V. K. R. V. Rao (1931–32). The National Income Committee was set up in 1949 under P. C. Mahalanobis.

question: Former Governor of Jharkhand from the year 2004 to 2009, __________, passed away in Lucknow in 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Syed Sibtey Razi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Syed Sibtey Razi served as the Governor of Jharkhand from 2004 to 2009. He passed away in Lucknow in 2022. (सैयद सिब्ते रजी)

• A veteran Indian National Congress leader from Uttar Pradesh, he was a member of both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha before becoming Governor, and also held additional charge as Governor of Assam for a period.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ramesh Bais served as Governor of Tripura (2019–2021), Jharkhand (2021–2023) and later Maharashtra.

• Syed Ahmed was Governor of Jharkhand (2011–2015) and earlier of Manipur.

• Kateekal Sankaranarayanan was Governor of Jharkhand (2009–2010) and of Maharashtra (2010–2014).

NOTE

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 (the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda), becoming India's 28th state; its capital is Ranchi.

• The Governor is appointed by the President under Article 155 and holds office during the President's pleasure (Article 156), normally for a term of five years.

question: According to the IUPAC nomenclature system, which functional group is characterised by the presence of a −OH group, usually in a water-like bent shape?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alcohols.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alcohols are the class of organic compounds characterised by the hydroxyl functional group (−OH) attached to a carbon atom. The C−O−H arrangement is bent (angular), much like the shape of a water (H₂O) molecule, because of the two lone pairs on oxygen. (एल्कोहॉल — हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह)

• In IUPAC nomenclature, alcohols take the suffix "-ol" — e.g. methanol (CH₃OH), ethanol (C₂H₅OH), propan-1-ol.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Carbonyls" contain the >C=O group — aldehydes (suffix -al) and ketones (suffix -one).

• Option 2 "Amines" contain the −NH₂ (amino) group — suffix -amine.

• Option 4 "Esters" contain the −COO− group — named as alkyl alkanoate, e.g. ethyl ethanoate; they give fruity smells.

NOTE

• Alcohols are classified as primary, secondary and tertiary depending on the number of carbon atoms attached to the carbon bearing the −OH group.

• Ethanol is the alcohol present in alcoholic drinks and is used in the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme; methanol is highly toxic and can cause blindness.

• IUPAC = International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, founded in 1919.

question: Ajmer Sharif is the shrine of which of the following Sufi saints?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ajmer Sharif Dargah in Ajmer, Rajasthan, is the tomb (shrine) of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (1141–1236), the founder of the Chishti Silsila (order) of Sufism in India. (ख्वाजा मोइनुद्दीन चिश्ती)

• He is popularly called "Gharib Nawaz" (benefactor of the poor). The annual "Urs" festival at his dargah attracts pilgrims of all faiths.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Muhammad Ghori — the Turkish invader who defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192); not a Sufi saint.

• Option 2 Muhammad bin Tughlaq — Delhi Sultan (1325–1351) known for transferring the capital to Daulatabad and introducing token currency.

• Option 4 Bakhtiyar Khilji — the general who invaded Bengal and destroyed Nalanda University.

NOTE

• Other important Chishti saints: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (Delhi), Baba Fariduddin Ganjshakar (Punjab), Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi) and Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi.

• Major Sufi silsilas in India: Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, Naqshbandi.

• Akbar was a devotee of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti and made pilgrimages to Ajmer on foot.

question: Whose autobiography is titled as ‘Wings of Fire: An Autobiography’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is APJ Abdul Kalam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wings of Fire: An Autobiography" (1999) was written by Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, co-authored with Arun Tiwari. It traces his journey from Rameswaram to India's missile and space programmes. (अग्नि की उड़ान — ए पी जे अब्दुल कलाम)

• Dr. Kalam served as the 11th President of India (2002–2007) and is called the "Missile Man of India" and the "People's President".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other books by Dr. Kalam: "India 2020: A Vision for the New Millennium", "Ignited Minds", "My Journey", "Turning Points", "Transcendence".

• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1981), Padma Vibhushan (1990) and Bharat Ratna (1997). His birthday, 15 October, is observed as World Students' Day.

• He was the chief architect of India's Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) and played a key role in Pokhran-II (1998), and earlier in the SLV-III launch that put Rohini into orbit (1980).

NOTE

• Option 1 E. Sreedharan — the "Metro Man of India", who led the Konkan Railway and Delhi Metro projects.

• Option 3 Rajendra Singh — the "Waterman of India", Ramon Magsaysay (2001) and Stockholm Water Prize (2015) winner.

• Option 4 Satyabhama Das Biju — the "Frogman of India", a noted amphibian biologist.

question: Which of the following Carnatic musicians was the first to receive the Bharat Ratna?
solution_text:
The correct answer is MS Subbulakshmi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• M. S. Subbulakshmi (1916–2004), the legendary Carnatic vocalist, became the first musician of any kind to be awarded the Bharat Ratna, in 1998. (एम एस सुब्बुलक्ष्मी)

• She was also the first Indian musician to perform at the United Nations General Assembly (1966) and the first Indian musician to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1974).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Born in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, she is remembered for the "Suprabhatam", "Vishnu Sahasranama" and bhajans such as Vaishnava Jana To. Mahatma Gandhi requested her rendition of Vaishnava Jana To, and Jawaharlal Nehru called her the "Queen of Song".

• Her other honours: Padma Bhushan (1954), Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1956), Padma Vibhushan (1975) and the Sangeetha Kalanidhi (1968) — she was the first woman to receive it.

NOTE

• Options 1 and 3 — Tyagaraja and Syama Sastri, along with Muthuswami Dikshitar, form the "Trinity of Carnatic Music" (18th–19th century); the Bharat Ratna did not exist in their time (it was instituted in 1954).

• Option 4 K. J. Yesudas is a celebrated playback singer and Carnatic musician awarded the Padma Vibhushan (2017), but not the Bharat Ratna.

• Other musicians awarded the Bharat Ratna: Ustad Bismillah Khan (2001), Pandit Ravi Shankar (1999), Bhimsen Joshi (2008) and Lata Mangeshkar (2001).

question: Which of the following is the highest navigable lake in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Titicaca.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lake Titicaca, lying on the border of Peru and Bolivia in the Andes mountains at an altitude of about 3,812 metres (12,507 ft), is the highest navigable lake in the world. (टिटिकाका झील)

• It is also the largest freshwater lake in South America by volume, with an area of about 8,372 km².

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Lake Huron and Option 3 Lake Superior are two of the five Great Lakes of North America (Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario — remembered by the acronym HOMES). Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.

• Option 4 Lake Como is a scenic glacial lake in northern Italy.

• The Uros people live on famous floating reed islands on Lake Titicaca; the lake's outlet is the Desaguadero river.

NOTE

• Other lake superlatives: Caspian Sea — largest lake in the world (saline); Lake Baikal (Russia) — deepest and oldest freshwater lake; Dead Sea — lowest point on land and one of the saltiest water bodies; Lake Assal (Djibouti) — lowest point in Africa.

question: Rukmini Devi Arundale was associated with which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (1904–1986) was the great revivalist of Bharatanatyam, who brought the dance out of the temple tradition and gave it respectability on the modern stage. (रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल — भरतनाट्यम)

• In 1936 she founded "Kalakshetra" at Adyar, Chennai, an institution devoted to the teaching of classical dance and music; the style taught there is known as the Kalakshetra bani (style).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She was the first woman to be nominated to the Rajya Sabha (1952) and was offered the post of President of India in 1977, which she declined.

• Honours: Padma Bhushan (1956), Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1957) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (1967). She was also a noted animal-welfare activist and piloted the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960.

NOTE

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni; other exponents include Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam and Mallika Sarabhai.

• The other options — Manipuri (Manipur; exponents: Guru Bipin Singh, Jhaveri sisters), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh; Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi), Mohiniyattam (Kerala; Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, Sunanda Nair).
